message.reasoning:
I need to bid on Tennessee Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

p2 has $844 cash and owns St. James and New York. He can build on the orange set. p3 has $803. I have $545. I will bid $341 to win.

I will drop out. p2 can still afford the orange set. I do not own any orange properties, so winning Tennessee would not complete a set for me.

Denying p2 an orange monopoly is the main goal. I am weighing whether to bid higher to push the price up or let p3 win at $340.

Owning Tennessee would leave me with only $204 cash. That is too little for a future denial bid on Marvin Gardens. I will drop out now.

p3's bid jumped from $261 to $340. I am reconsidering whether to stay in and push the price higher, or drop out and let p3 win.

Dropping out is dangerous. p2 could bid $341 and p3 might drop, giving p2 the orange monopoly for $341 with $503 cash left to build immediately. I will stay in and bid just above $340 to keep pressure.

A $400 purchase leaves p2 with $444 cash. He could still build one house on each orange property for $300, leaving $144. That is dangerous but far less than buying at $180. I am checking the exact rent values to judge the risk.

Tennessee rent with three houses is $550. New York rent with three houses is $600. A $500 purchase leaves p2 with $344 cash, enough for three houses and $44 left over. That is painful but manageable. p3 has $803 and may be willing to bid $400–$500 to deny p2.

I will bid $341 to stay in and force the price up. A win would leave me with only $204 cash, which is too little to buy Marvin Gardens at face value later. Preventing p2 from completing an orange monopoly is more important than saving cash for Marvin.

A $400 purchase would leave me with only $145 cash and a useless dead asset. I will not bid that high. I will drop out and let p3 or p2 pay more to prevent p2 from completing an orange monopoly.

I will bid at least $341 to block p2 from sniping the property. I cannot predict whether p3 will continue bidding, so I must stay in and force the price higher.

I will bid $360 to block p2 from sniping at $341. I am staying near my $400 cap, so I can drop out if the price rises further.

A $400 jump would signal too much commitment and might scare p3. I will bid the minimum $341 to stay in cheaply. That price is 1.9 times face value, which is worth blocking an orange monopoly. p2 will almost certainly bid over $341.

A $400 bid might cause p3 to fold, leaving p2 to bid $401 and forcing me back into the auction. I will bid incrementally at $351 or $360 instead. I cannot trade Tennessee immediately to complete a set.

messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Swapping Atlantic Avenue for Ventnor Avenue is a lateral move on Yellow, so p4 is effectively offering $250 for Park Place (which costs $350 and gives me half of the Dark Blue set with Boardwalk still unowned). I already have $826 cash and have no reason to sell Park Place at a discount. Rejecting.

Giving p2 Park Place completes their Dark Blue monopoly while they have $613 cash to build immediately, whereas St. Charles Place and Pennsylvania Avenue leave me without any completed set (since p4 holds States Avenue). I will not hand out a monopoly without getting a completed monopoly in return. Rejecting.

Paid $10 rent on States Avenue. I have $816 cash (the highest at the table) and am positioned right before the remaining unowned properties (Tennessee, B&O, Marvin Gardens, Pacific, Short Line). Holding onto my cash and properties for now. Ending turn.

Paid $16 rent on New York Avenue. With $800 cash and unowned properties (B&O Railroad, Marvin Gardens, Pacific Avenue, Short Line) directly ahead of me, there is no beneficial two-player trade to make right now. Ending turn.

Landed on my own Atlantic Avenue. p1 now has the Red monopoly with 1 house each and $19 cash. No two-player trade currently gives me a strong completed monopoly since Pink is split three ways, Yellow still has Marvin Gardens unowned 3 spaces ahead of me, and p2 has no reason to sell Boardwalk without getting a monopoly in return. Holding my $800 cash and ending turn.

Paid $26 rent on Pacific Avenue and still hold $809 cash. No two-player trade can yield a worthwhile monopoly right now since Pink is split three ways, Yellow and Orange still have unowned properties, and neither p2 nor I can give the other an alternative monopoly for Dark Blue. Ending turn.

Paid $50 rent on Boardwalk and have $803 cash with GO right ahead. No two-player trade yields a worthwhile monopoly right now since Pink is split three ways, Yellow and Orange still have unowned properties, and neither p2 nor I can offer a completed monopoly for Dark Blue. Ending turn.

Swapping Virginia Avenue for States Avenue is a slight downgrade on Pink, and selling Atlantic Avenue for $250 (below its $260 face value) would give p4 two of the three Yellow properties with Marvin Gardens still unowned. I already have $803 cash and have no reason to help p4 consolidate Yellow. Rejecting.

p2 holds St. James and New York Avenue with $844 cash. Letting p2 get Tennessee Avenue cheap would give them an immediate Orange monopoly with plenty of cash to build houses. Winning Tennessee also gives me direct leverage to trade with p2 for Boardwalk, and I am on Boardwalk guaranteed to pass GO for $200 next turn. Bidding $250.

p2 has $844 cash and the other two Oranges. Letting p2 win Tennessee Avenue for $261 gives them an instant Orange monopoly with ~$580 left to build houses. Winning Tennessee also gives me direct trade leverage for p2's Boardwalk (since I hold Park Place), and I am on Boardwalk guaranteed to collect $200 for passing GO on my next roll. Bidding $340.
